observations.summary: The first macOS validation attempt errored in the timeout process-tree test when final cleanup called killpg and received EPERM.
The rerun reproduced the same macOS test, call site, and EPERM exception on the same exact revision.

success_criteria: A deterministic regression reproduces the post-timeout final-cleanup failure without relying on runner timing.
POSIX cleanup is idempotent only after successful termination while an initial inability to terminate remains fail-closed.
The timeout regression still fails if the child or any descendant survives.
Focused process-boundary tests pass repeatedly on macOS and Gate A passes on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.

monitoring_plan.criterion: After promotion, repeated macOS timeout trials finish without cleanup errors and prove that the complete created process tree is gone.

lesson.reason: A deterministic post-timeout cleanup seam plus a descendant-survival regression is the intended durable control; no candidate or promotion is claimed by this intake record.

disposition_reason: Recorded at observed after the same macOS failure fingerprint recurred on an exact-head rerun. The byte-identical merge tree later passed, so the evidence establishes nondeterminism but not a repair; lifecycle promotion remains external.
limitations: The failure was observed only on GitHub-hosted macOS and did not reproduce on the byte-identical main run.
No local macOS runner or deterministic process-group seam was available during closeout.
The exact safe interpretation of EPERM after termination has not been decided.
Only the schema layer is enforced while the semantic improvement validators remain parked.
No candidate revision, evaluation envelope, independent review, merge, or monitoring evidence exists yet.

Repair prepared 2026-08-15 from 0104b55, not evaluated. The POSIX final close now tolerates EPERM only when the group leader is already reaped (process.poll() is not None), which is the one state where the call is a re-run of completed work. While the process is still running, EPERM means the tree was not signalled and a descendant may be alive, so it raises process-tree-boundary-failed. The initial _terminate_process_tree never tolerates EPERM and now raises the same boundary code the Windows branch uses instead of letting a bare OSError be reinterpreted upstream as a launch failure. ProcessLookupError handling is unchanged. Evidence: docs/reviews/2026-08-15-posix-boundary-cleanup-repair.md.

The regression set is deterministic and distinguishes the correct fix from the unsafe one. Reverting to no PermissionError handling gives 2 errors (the shipped defect); reverting to an unconditional swallow -- the broad catch the intake packet warns against -- gives 1 failure; making the initial termination tolerate EPERM gives 1 failure. A regression set that only proved the reported error stops happening would have been satisfied by the unsafe repair. The new tests use a mocked os.killpg and a stubbed poll(), so they involve no real processes, no sleeps, and no runner timing; they are skipped on Windows where the POSIX path is unreachable and a pass would be vacuous. The pre-existing real-process descendant assertions are retained unchanged and remain the control that would catch a survivor.

Success criterion 4 is NOT met and cannot be met from this environment: focused process-boundary tests passing repeatedly on macOS requires the CI matrix on the exact candidate. Linux evidence only: five consecutive ProcessBoundaryTests runs and six consecutive full-file runs green, plus Gate A 39/39 on the pinned Python 3.12. Separately, that macOS returns EPERM for the assumed reason is not confirmed by observation -- the repair is scoped by process state rather than by a theory of the kernel, so it is correct for any EPERM arriving after the leader is reaped.

evals/codex_trial.py is a pinned member of the nine-file evaluator bundle, so its digest and size were refreshed in codex-terra-evaluator-v1.json; Gate A caught the stale row before it could ship. Exactly one row changed. The scenario, routing manifest, frozen scenario digests, and trial shape are untouched, and no live Terra trial, canary, or campaign was run. No attempt is appended and the status stays observed: an attempt's evaluation must be a fresh evidence envelope produced outside the authoring checkout, which the author cannot supply for itself.

Correction from independent review on PR #114, confirmed before acting: the first repair inferred 'already terminated' from the leader being reaped, which is wrong. On every normal-completion path _terminate_process_tree is never called, so the final close is the first and only kill of the group and is what removes a descendant the leader spawned before exiting; an EPERM there was silently accepted and the descendant escaped the boundary. Tolerance now requires a prior successful kill AND a reaped leader, with the fact threaded from each termination call site and defaulting to False. The candidate revision is 13e6fd4d3f355b0c3c366d999fc8537c4356c3ac; the earlier ledger text pinned base 0104b55, which contains none of the repair and must not be evaluated as the candidate.
